formulaCard.title: Sinking Fund Payment

explanation: A [[kw:sinking fund]] is a fund established to accumulate a specific future sum by making equal periodic deposits.
It is the reverse of the future value of an ordinary annuity: you know the target FV, and you calculate the required periodic payment.
The payment is made at the end of each period (ordinary annuity) unless stated otherwise.
Formula: $$\text{Payment} = \frac{FV}{\text{FV Annuity Factor}}$$ or using a sinking fund table factor: $$\text{Payment} = FV \times \text{Sinking Fund Factor}$$.
[[imp:The sinking fund factor is the reciprocal of the ordinary annuity FV factor.]]

explanation: A [[kw:sinking fund table]] lists factors that, when multiplied by the future value, give the required periodic payment.
Factor = $\frac{i}{(1+i)^n - 1}$, the reciprocal of the FV ordinary annuity factor.
Steps: 1. Compute i and n. 2. Find the factor at the intersection of n (row) and i (column). 3. Payment = FV × Factor.
The factor is always less than 1 and decreases as i increases (due to compounding).
[[imp:If only the ordinary annuity table is available, the sinking fund factor = 1 ÷ FV annuity factor.]]

notes: Factor is found in the sinking fund table.

explanation: To verify the sinking fund payment, create an accumulation schedule:
Start with $0.

For each period: 1. Add the sinking fund deposit. 2. Add interest on the previous balance (interest is calculated before the deposit for end-of-period deposits?). Wait, in a sinking fund, deposits are at the end, so interest is calculated on the balance before adding the new deposit. So the process: Interest = previous balance × i. New balance = previous balance + interest + deposit.
After n periods, the balance should equal the target FV.
[[imp:This check confirms that the payment correctly accumulates to the desired future sum.]]

blocks.title: 3. Checking Sinking Fund by Accumulation

discoveryHook.scenario: After calculating the required annual deposit, you can verify it by simulating the fund: each year, add the deposit, then add interest on the previous balance. After the last deposit (which earns no interest), the total should equal the target.

If you know you can save $200/month for 18 years, an ordinary annuity tells you the future value. If you have a target of $50,000, a sinking fund tells you the required monthly deposit. They are two sides of the same coin.

formulaCard.formula: $$\text{FV Annuity Factor} \times \text{Sinking Fund Factor} = 1$$ $$\text{Payment (SF)} = \frac{FV}{\text{FV Annuity Factor}}$$
formulaCard.title: Key Relationships
notes: If you have the ordinary annuity table, you can find sinking fund payments.
If you have the sinking fund table, you can find FV of ordinary annuity.

explanation: Ordinary annuity: $FV = \text{Payment} \times \text{FV Annuity Factor}$ (unknown FV).
Sinking fund: $\text{Payment} = FV \times \text{Sinking Fund Factor}$ (unknown payment).
The sinking fund factor is the reciprocal of the FV annuity factor: $\text{SF Factor} = \frac{1}{\text{FV Annuity Factor}}$.
Both use end-of-period payments and the same i and n.
[[imp:Choose the correct formula based on whether FV or payment is the unknown.]]

explanation: Apply the blueprint to sinking fund problems:
1. Understand: identify target FV, annual rate, compounding frequency, and number of years.
2. Solve: compute n and i; find sinking fund factor from table or compute as 1 / FV annuity factor; Payment = FV × Factor.
3. Conclude: verify by building an accumulation schedule; state the required periodic deposit.
This ensures you use the correct factor and check your result.
